title.zh: 卷一百一十 列傳第四十: 姦臣上
title.raw: 卷一百一十 列傳第四十: 姦臣上 Volume 110 Biographies 40: Treacherous Ministers 1

sentences.zh: 奸臣上 ○耶律乙辛張孝傑耶律燕哥蕭十三

translations.literal: Treacherous Ministers 1 ○ Yelü Yixin, Zhang Xiaojie, Yelü Yangge, Xiao Shisan
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous Ministers, Part 1 ○ Yelü Yixin, Zhang Xiaojie, Yelü Yangge, and Xiao Shisan

sentences.zh: 《春秋》褒貶，善惡並書，示勸懲也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals both praise and blame, recording good and evil together, to show encouragement and warning.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, praise and blame appear side by side, and good and evil are recorded together, so that readers may be encouraged or warned.

sentences.zh: 故遷、固傳佞幸、酷吏，歐陽修則並奸臣錄之，將俾為君者知所鑒，為臣者知所戒。

translations.literal: Therefore Sima Qian and Ban Gu wrote biographies of flatterers and harsh officials; Ouyang Xiu also included treacherous ministers, intending that rulers might know what to take as a mirror and ministers what to take as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Sima Qian and Ban Gu devoted biographies to flatterers and harsh officials, and why Ouyang Xiu added treacherous ministers as well—so that rulers would know what to heed and ministers what to fear.

sentences.zh: 此天地聖賢之心，國家安危之機，治亂之原也。

translations.literal: This is the mind of Heaven and earth and the sages, the pivot of a state's safety and peril, and the source of order and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Such writing reflects the intent of Heaven, earth, and the sages; it touches the hinge on which a state's safety turns and the root from which order and chaos spring.

sentences.zh: 遼自耶律乙辛而下，奸臣十人，其敗國皆足以為戒，故列於《傳》。

translations.literal: From Yelü Yixin downward in Liao there were ten treacherous ministers; each ruined the state in ways sufficient to serve as a warning, and so they are set down in the Biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liao, from Yelü Yixin onward there were ten such ministers, each of whose ruinous careers is warning enough to be recorded in the Biographies.

sentences.zh: 耶律乙辛，字胡睹袞，五院部人。

translations.literal: Yelü Yixin, courtesy name Hudugun, was a man of the Five-Yuan Division.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yixin, whose courtesy name was Hudugun, came from the Five-Yuan Division.

sentences.zh: 父叠剌，家貧，服用不給，部人號「窮叠剌」。

translations.literal: His father Yela was poor and could not supply clothing and food; the people of the division called him "Poor Yela."
translations.idiomatic: His father Yela was so poor that the family could scarcely keep clothed and fed, and their clansmen nicknamed him "Poor Yela."

sentences.zh: 初，乙辛母方娠，夜夢手搏羖羊，拔其角尾。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Yixin's mother was pregnant, she dreamed at night that she wrestled with a ram and pulled off its horns and tail.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was born, his mother dreamed that she grappled with a ram and tore off its horns and tail.

sentences.zh: 既寤占之，術者曰：「此吉兆也。

translations.literal: When she awoke she had it divined; the practitioner said, "This is an auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: On waking she had the dream interpreted, and the diviner said, "This is a fortunate sign.

sentences.zh: 羊去角尾為王字，汝後有子當王。」

translations.literal: When the ram loses horns and tail it forms the character for 'king'; you will later have a son who will become king."
translations.idiomatic: A ram stripped of horn and tail leaves the character for 'king'; you will bear a son who is destined for kingship."

sentences.zh: 及乙辛生，適在路，無水以浴，回車破轍，忽見湧泉。

translations.literal: When Yixin was born they happened to be on the road with no water for bathing; they turned the cart and broke the rut, and suddenly a spring gushed forth.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixin was born they were still on the road and had no water for the birth-bath; they turned the cart back, the wheel broke through the track, and a spring suddenly welled up.

sentences.zh: 叠剌自以得子，欲酒以慶，聞酒香，於草棘間得二榼，因祭東焉。

translations.literal: Yela, taking himself to have gained a son, wished wine to celebrate; smelling wine, he found two jars among grass and thorns and therefore made offering to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Yela, overjoyed at having a son, wanted wine for a celebration; catching the scent of wine, he found two jars among the brush and offered sacrifice to the east.

sentences.zh: 乙辛幼慧黠。

translations.literal: Yixin in youth was clever and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Yixin was clever and quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 嘗牧羊至日昃，叠剌視之，乙辛熟寢。

translations.literal: Once he was herding sheep until the sun slanted; Yela went to look and Yixin was sleeping soundly.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while herding sheep until late in the day, he was found by Yela fast asleep.

sentences.zh: 叠剌觸之覺，乙辛怒曰：「何遽驚我！

translations.literal: Yela touched him and he awoke; Yixin angrily said, "Why startle me so suddenly!
translations.idiomatic: Yela roused him with a touch, and Yixin snapped, "Why wake me so abruptly!

sentences.zh: 適夢人手執日月以食我，我已食月，啖日方半而覺，惜不盡食之。」

translations.literal: I was just dreaming that a person's hand held the sun and moon to feed me; I had already eaten the moon and was halfway through eating the sun when I awoke, regretting that I had not finished eating them."
translations.idiomatic: I was dreaming that someone was feeding me the sun and moon—I had already swallowed the moon and was halfway through the sun when you woke me. I regret not finishing the meal.

sentences.zh: 叠剌自是不令牧羊。

translations.literal: From then on Yela no longer had him herd sheep.
translations.idiomatic: After that Yela never sent him out to herd sheep again.

sentences.zh: 大康元年，皇太子始預朝政，法度修明。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dakang, the crown prince first took part in court government, and laws and standards were put in good order.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Dakang era, the crown prince began to take part in government, and regulations were enforced with new rigor.

sentences.zh: 乙辛不得逞，謀以事誣皇后。

translations.literal: Yixin could not have his way and plotted to frame the empress on a charge.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to have his way, Yixin plotted to frame the empress on a false charge.

sentences.zh: 后既死，乙辛不自安，又欲害太子。

translations.literal: After the empress died, Yixin was ill at ease and again wished to harm the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress was dead, Yixin grew uneasy and turned his mind again to destroying the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 乘間入奏曰：「帝與后如天地並位，中宮豈可曠？」

translations.literal: Seizing an opportunity he entered and memorialized, saying, "Emperor and empress stand like Heaven and earth side by side—how can the inner palace stand empty?"
translations.idiomatic: Seizing a moment to address the throne, he said, "Emperor and empress stand together like Heaven and earth—how can the inner palace be left vacant?

sentences.zh: 盛稱其黨駙馬都尉蕭霞抹之妹美而賢。

translations.literal: He lavishly praised the sister of his partisan, Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Xiao Xiamo, as beautiful and worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He then spoke at length of the beauty and virtue of the sister of his ally, Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Xiao Xiamo.

sentences.zh: 上信之，納於宮，尋冊為皇后。

translations.literal: The emperor believed him, took her into the palace, and soon enfeoffed her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him, brought the woman into the palace, and soon installed her as empress.

sentences.zh: 時護衛蕭忽古知乙辛奸狀，伏橋下，欲殺之。

translations.literal: At that time the guardsman Xiao Hugu knew Yixin's treacherous conduct, lay in wait under a bridge, and wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The guardsman Xiao Hugu, who knew Yixin's treachery, lay in ambush beneath a bridge intending to kill him.

sentences.zh: 俄暴雨壞橋，謀不遂。

translations.literal: Soon a violent rainstorm destroyed the bridge, and the plot did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden downpour wrecked the bridge, and the plot came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 林牙蕭巖壽密奏曰：「乙辛自皇太子預政，內懷疑懼，又與宰相張孝傑相附會。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Xiao Yanshou secretly memorialized, saying, "Since the crown prince began to share in government, Yixin has harbored suspicion and fear within, and moreover he has joined forces with the chief minister Zhang Xiaojie.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Xiao Yanshou submitted a secret memorial: "Ever since the crown prince entered government, Yixin has been inwardly fearful, and he has been in league with Chief Minister Zhang Xiaojie.

sentences.zh: 恐有異圖，不可使居要地。」

translations.literal: I fear he has ulterior designs and he must not be allowed to hold a crucial post."
translations.idiomatic: I fear he harbors ulterior designs; he must not be left in a position of power.

sentences.zh: 出為中京留守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Military Governor of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin was transferred out to serve as Military Governor of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 乙辛泣謂人曰：「乙辛無過，因讒見出。」

translations.literal: Yixin wept and said to others, "Yixin has no fault; it is because of slander that I have been sent out."
translations.idiomatic: Yixin wept and told others, "I have done nothing wrong; it is slander that has driven me out.

sentences.zh: 其黨蕭霞抹輩以其言聞於上。

translations.literal: His partisans Xiao Xiamo and the like reported his words to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His partisans, including Xiao Xiamo, repeated these words to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上悔之。

translations.literal: The emperor regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to regret the decision.

sentences.zh: 無何，出蕭巖壽為順義軍節度使，詔近臣議召乙辛事。

translations.literal: Before long, Xiao Yanshou was sent out as Military Commissioner of the Shunyi Army, and an edict ordered close ministers to discuss recalling Yixin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiao Yanshou was posted away as Military Commissioner of the Shunyi Army, and the emperor ordered his close advisers to deliberate on recalling Yixin.

sentences.zh: 北面官屬無敢言者，耶律撒剌曰：「初以蕭巖壽奏出乙辛，若所言不當，宜坐以罪，若當，則不可復召。」

translations.literal: Among the Northern Court officials none dared speak; Yelü Sala said, "At first Yixin was sent out on Xiao Yanshou's memorial—if what he said was improper, he should be punished for a crime; if it was proper, then Yixin must not be recalled."
translations.idiomatic: None of the Northern Court officials dared speak up until Yelü Sala said, "Yixin was removed on Xiao Yanshou's memorial. If that memorial was wrong, Yanshou should be punished; if it was right, Yixin must not be brought back.

sentences.zh: 累諫不從。

translations.literal: He remonstrated repeatedly but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated again and again, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 乃復召為北院樞密使。

translations.literal: Yixin was then recalled and made Commissioner of the Northern Commissioner's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin was nevertheless recalled and reappointed Commissioner of the Northern Commissioner's Office.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子以母後之故，憂見顏色。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince, on account of his mother's death, showed grief in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, grieving his mother's death, wore sorrow plain on his face.

sentences.zh: 乙辛黨欣躍相慶，讒謗沸騰，忠良之士，斥逐殆盡。

translations.literal: Yixin's faction leaped for joy and congratulated one another; slander boiled over, and loyal and good men were driven out almost to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin's faction rejoiced openly while slander swirled through the court and loyal officials were driven out almost to a man.

sentences.zh: 乙辛因蕭十三之言，夜召蕭得裏特謀構太子，令護衛太保耶律查剌誣告耶律撒剌等同謀立皇太子。

translations.literal: On Xiao Shisan's words, Yixin by night summoned Xiao Delite to plot framing the crown prince, and ordered Guards Commissioner Yelü Chala to lodge a false accusation that Yelü Sala and others had conspired to install the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on Xiao Shisan's counsel, Yixin summoned Xiao Delite by night to plot against the crown prince and had Guards Commissioner Yelü Chala accuse Yelü Sala and others of conspiring to put the prince on the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔按無跡而罷。

translations.literal: An edict ordered investigation; no trace was found and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: An investigation ordered by edict found no evidence, and the case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 又令牌印郎君蕭訛都斡詣上誣首：「耶律查剌前告耶律撒剌等事皆實，臣亦與其謀。

translations.literal: He again ordered Seal-and-Token Gentleman Xiao Eduo to go before the emperor with a false confession: "Yelü Chala's earlier accusation against Yelü Sala and the rest was all true, and I too took part in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Seal-and-Token Gentleman Xiao Eduo appear before the throne with a fabricated confession: "Yelü Chala's earlier charge against Yelü Sala and the others was true, and I was party to the plot as well.

sentences.zh: 本欲殺乙辛等而立太子。

translations.literal: We originally intended to kill Yixin and the rest and establish the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Our plan was to kill Yixin and his faction and set up the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 臣等若不言，恐事白連坐。」

translations.literal: If we ministers did not speak, I feared that when the affair came to light we would be implicated together."
translations.idiomatic: If we kept silent, we feared we would be punished together once the plot was exposed.

sentences.zh: 詔使鞫劾，乙辛迫令具伏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered interrogation; Yixin forced them to confess in full.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an inquiry, and Yixin tortured the accused until they confessed.

sentences.zh: 上怒，命誅撒剌及速撒等。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and ordered the execution of Sala, Susa, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor ordered Sala, Susa, and the others put to death.

sentences.zh: 乙辛恐帝疑，引數人庭詰，各令荷重校，繩系其頸，不能出氣，人人不堪其酷，惟求速死。

translations.literal: Yixin feared the emperor's doubts; he brought several men into the courtyard for questioning, had each bear heavy cangues, and bound ropes about their necks so they could not breathe; every man could not endure the cruelty and only begged to die quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the emperor's doubts, Yixin had several men questioned in the courtyard, loaded with heavy cangues and ropes drawn tight about their necks until they could scarcely breathe; broken by the torment, each man begged only for a swift death.

sentences.zh: 反奏曰：「別無異辭。」

translations.literal: He instead memorialized, saying, "There is no other testimony."
translations.idiomatic: He then reported back, "They have nothing further to say.

sentences.zh: 時方暑，屍不得瘞，以至地臭。

translations.literal: It was then midsummer; the corpses could not be buried, until the ground reeked.
translations.idiomatic: It was high summer, and the bodies could not be buried in time; the stench filled the ground.

sentences.zh: 乃囚皇太子於上京，監衛者皆其黨。

translations.literal: The crown prince was then imprisoned at the Supreme Capital; all the supervising guards were his partisans.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was imprisoned at the Supreme Capital under guards who were all Yixin's men.

sentences.zh: 尋遣蕭達魯古、撒把害太子。

translations.literal: Soon Xiao Dalugu and Saba were sent to harm the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xiao Dalugu and Saba were dispatched to murder the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 乙辛黨大喜，聚飲數日。

translations.literal: Yixin's faction was greatly pleased and gathered to drink for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin's faction celebrated with feasting that lasted for days.

sentences.zh: 上京留守蕭撻得以卒聞。

translations.literal: The Military Governor of the Supreme Capital, Xiao Tade, was able to report the death in full.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tade, Military Governor of the Supreme Capital, was able to report the prince's death in detail.

sentences.zh: 上哀悼，欲召其妻，乙辛陰遣人殺之，以滅其口。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned and wished to summon the prince's wife; Yixin secretly sent men to kill her, to silence witnesses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned and wished to summon the prince's wife, but Yixin secretly had her killed to silence anyone who might speak.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，上將出獵，乙辛奏留皇孫，上欲從之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, when the emperor was about to go hunting, Yixin memorialized to keep the imperial grandson behind; the emperor wished to agree.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, as the emperor prepared to go hunting, Yixin asked that the imperial grandson be left behind, and the emperor was inclined to agree.

sentences.zh: 同知點檢蕭兀納諫曰：「陛下若從乙辛留皇孫，皇孫尚幼，左右無人，願留臣保護，以防不測。」

translations.literal: Associate Commissioner of the Palace Inspection Office Xiao Wuna remonstrated, saying, "If Your Majesty follows Yixin in keeping the imperial grandson, the grandson is still young and will have no one at his side; I beg to remain to protect him, to guard against the unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: Associate Commissioner of the Palace Inspection Office Xiao Wuna remonstrated: "If Your Majesty leaves the grandson behind as Yixin wishes, he is still a child with no one trustworthy at his side. Allow me to stay and guard him against mishap.

sentences.zh: 遂與皇孫俱行。

translations.literal: He then went together with the imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the grandson with him on the hunt.

sentences.zh: 由是上始疑乙辛，頗知其奸。

translations.literal: From this the emperor first grew suspicious of Yixin and came to know his treachery fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: From this the emperor first began to suspect Yixin and to see something of his treachery.

sentences.zh: 會北幸，將次黑山之平澱，上適見扈從官屬多隨乙辛後，惡之，出乙辛知南院大王事。

translations.literal: When the emperor was on a northern tour and was about to halt at the Pingdian of Black Mountain, he happened to see that many of the attendant officials followed behind Yixin; he disliked this and sent Yixin out to serve as Grand Prince of the Southern Commission.
translations.idiomatic: On a tour of the north, as the court was about to encamp at the Pingdian ford on Black Mountain, the emperor noticed how many attendants trailed behind Yixin and took offense; Yixin was transferred to the post of Grand Prince of the Southern Commission.

sentences.zh: 及例削一字王爵，改王混同，意稍自安。

translations.literal: When by precedent one character was cut from his princely title and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Huntong, his mind grew somewhat at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When, by the usual rule, one character was stripped from his princely title and he was redesignated Prince of Huntong, he felt somewhat reassured.

sentences.zh: 及赴闕入謝，帝即日遣還，改知興中府事。

translations.literal: When he came to the capital to enter thanks, the emperor that same day sent him back and changed his appointment to Administrator of the Xingzhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court to offer thanks, the emperor sent him back the same day and reassigned him as Administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，坐以禁物鬻入外國，下有司議，法當死。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year he was charged with selling forbidden goods into foreign states; the matter was referred to the relevant offices for deliberation, and by law he should die.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year he was convicted of selling contraband abroad; the case was referred to the judicial offices, and the statute called for death.

sentences.zh: 乙辛黨耶律燕哥獨奏當入八議，得減死論，擊以鐵骨朵，幽於來州。

translations.literal: Yixin's partisan Yelü Yangge alone memorialized that he should enter the Eight Deliberations, and a reduced sentence from death was obtained; he was struck with the iron mace and confined at Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin's ally Yelü Yangge alone argued that the Eight Deliberations should apply; the sentence was reduced from death, Yixin was beaten with the iron mace, and imprisoned at Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 後謀奔宋及私藏兵甲事覺，縊殺之。

translations.literal: Later his plot to flee to Song and his private hoard of weapons and armor came to light, and he was strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his plot to flee to Song and his secret store of arms were discovered, he was strangled.

sentences.zh: 乾統二年，發冢，戮其屍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiantong his tomb was opened and his corpse was disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiantong his tomb was opened and his corpse was publicly shamed.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，乙辛譖皇太子，孝傑同力相濟。

translations.literal: That summer Yixin slandered the crown prince, and Xiaojie lent his strength in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when Yixin slandered the crown prince, Xiaojie worked hand in hand with him.

sentences.zh: 及乙辛受詔按皇太子黨人，誣害忠良，孝傑之謀居多。

translations.literal: When Yixin received the edict to investigate the crown prince's partisans and falsely harmed the loyal and good, Xiaojie's schemes made up the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixin was ordered to investigate the crown prince's supposed faction and framed loyal men, most of the plotting came from Xiaojie.

sentences.zh: 乙辛薦孝傑忠於社稷，帝謂孝傑可比狄仁傑，賜名仁傑，乃許放海東青鶻。

translations.literal: Yixin recommended Xiaojie as loyal to the altars of state; the emperor said Xiaojie could be compared to Di Renjie, bestowed the name Renjie, and then permitted the release of the eastern-sea green falcon.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin praised Xiaojie as loyal to the realm; the emperor compared him to Di Renjie, granted him the name Renjie, and allowed the eastern-sea green falcon to be sent forth.

sentences.zh: 六年，既出乙辛，上亦悟孝傑奸佞，尋出為武定軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, after Yixin had been sent out, the emperor also perceived Xiaojie's treachery and flattery, and soon sent him out as Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, once Yixin had been removed, the emperor also saw through Xiaojie's treachery and soon posted him away as Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army.

sentences.zh: 坐私販廣濟湖鹽及擅改詔旨，削爵，貶安肅州，數年乃歸。

translations.literal: He was charged with privately trafficking salt from Guangji Lake and altering an edict on his own authority; his noble rank was stripped, he was demoted to Ansu Prefecture, and only after several years did he return.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of smuggling salt from Guangji Lake and altering an imperial edict on his own authority, he was stripped of rank, banished to Ansu Prefecture, and allowed to return only years later.

sentences.zh: 大安中，死於鄉。

translations.literal: In the Da'an era he died in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home during the Da'an era.

sentences.zh: 乾統初，剖棺戮屍，以族產分賜臣下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiantong his coffin was opened and his corpse disgraced, and his clan property was divided and bestowed on subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiantong his coffin was opened and his corpse shamed, and his family's property was divided among officials as gifts.

sentences.zh: 孝傑久在相位，貪貨無厭，時與親戚會飲，嘗曰：「無百萬兩黃金，不足為宰相家。」

translations.literal: Xiaojie long held the chancellorship, greedy for goods without satiety; he would meet with kinsmen to drink and once said, "Without a million taels of gold one is not fit to be a chancellor's household."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojie had long held the chancellorship and was insatiably greedy for wealth; drinking with his kinsmen he once remarked, "A million taels of gold is the least a chancellor's household deserves.

sentences.zh: 初，孝傑及第，詣佛寺，忽迅風吹孝傑襆頭，與浮圖齊，墜地而碎。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiaojie passed the examinations, he visited a Buddhist temple; suddenly a swift wind blew Xiaojie's headwrap level with the pagoda; it fell to the ground and shattered.
translations.idiomatic: When he first passed the examinations he visited a Buddhist temple; a sudden gust lifted his cap level with the pagoda, then dashed it to the ground where it shattered.

sentences.zh: 有老僧曰：「此人必驟貴，然亦不得其死。」

translations.literal: An old monk said, "This man will surely rise swiftly to high rank, yet he will also not die a natural death."
translations.idiomatic: An old monk said, "This man will rise swiftly to power, but he will not die a natural death.

sentences.zh: 竟如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it was exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it happened just as he had said.

sentences.zh: 耶律燕哥，字善寧，季父房之後。

translations.literal: Yelü Yangge, courtesy name Shaning, was a descendant of the Lesser Father House.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yangge, whose courtesy name was Shaning, was descended from the Lesser Father House.

sentences.zh: 四世祖鐸穩，太祖異母弟。

translations.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor Duowen was the Taizu Emperor's younger half-brother.
translations.idiomatic: His fourth-generation ancestor Duowen was a younger half-brother of Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 父曰豁裏斯，官至太師。

translations.literal: His father, named Huolisi, reached the office of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huolisi rose to the rank of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 燕哥狡佞而敏。

translations.literal: Yangge was crafty, fawning, and quick.
translations.idiomatic: Yangge was cunning, fawning, and quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 清寧間，為左護衛太保。

translations.literal: During Qingning he served as Left Guards Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingning era he served as Left Guards Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大康初，轉北面林牙。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dakang he was transferred to Northern Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Dakang era he was made Northern Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 初，耶律乙辛自中京留守復為樞密使，以燕哥為耳目，凡聞見必以告。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yelü Yixin returned from Military Governor of the Central Capital to Commissioner of the Commissioner's Office, he used Yangge as eyes and ears; whatever he heard or saw he always reported.
translations.idiomatic: When Yelü Yixin returned from the Central Capital to the Commissioner's Office, he used Yangge as his eyes and ears, reporting everything he heard or saw.

sentences.zh: 乙辛愛而薦之，帝亦以為賢，拜左夷離畢。

translations.literal: Yixin favored him and recommended him; the emperor also considered him worthy and appointed him Left Yilibi.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin favored and recommended him; the emperor too judged him worthy and appointed him Left Yilibi.

sentences.zh: 及皇太子被誣，帝遣燕哥往訊之，太子謂燕哥曰：「帝惟我一子，今為儲嗣，復何求，敢為此事！

translations.literal: When the crown prince was falsely accused, the emperor sent Yangge to interrogate him; the prince said to Yangge, "The emperor has only me as a son; I am now heir apparent—what more could I seek that I would dare do such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was framed, the emperor sent Yangge to question him. The prince said, "The emperor has only one son, and I am his heir—what could I possibly gain by such a plot!

sentences.zh: 公與我為昆弟行，當念無辜，達意於帝。」

translations.literal: You and I are as brothers in rank; you ought to think of my innocence and convey my meaning to the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: We stand as brothers in rank—think of my innocence and plead my case to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 禱之甚懇。

translations.literal: He prayed to him most earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: He begged him with desperate earnestness.

sentences.zh: 蕭十三聞之，謂燕哥曰：「宜以太子言易為伏狀。」

translations.literal: Xiao Shisan heard of it and said to Yangge, "You ought to turn the crown prince's words into a confession with ease."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Shisan heard of this he told Yangge, "Twist the prince's words into a confession.

sentences.zh: 燕哥頷之，盡如所教以奏。

translations.literal: Yangge nodded assent and memorialized exactly as instructed.
translations.idiomatic: Yangge agreed and reported to the throne exactly as he had been taught.

sentences.zh: 及太子被逐，乙辛殺害忠良，多燕哥之謀，為契丹行宮都部署。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was driven out, Yixin killed and harmed the loyal and good—much of it was Yangge's plotting—and he became Overall Deployer of the Khitan Traveling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince was banished, Yixin's slaughter of loyal officials owed much to Yangge's counsel; Yangge was made Overall Deployer of the Khitan Traveling Palace.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，拜南府宰相，遷惕隱。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year he was appointed Chancellor of the Southern Commission and transferred to Tiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year he was made Chancellor of the Southern Commission and then promoted to Tiyin.

sentences.zh: 大安三年，為西京留守，致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Da'an he served as Military Governor of the Western Capital and then retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Da'an he became Military Governor of the Western Capital, then retired from office.

sentences.zh: 壽隆初，以疾卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shoulong he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shoulong era he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 蕭十三，蔑古乃部人。

translations.literal: Xiao Shisan was a man of the Miegunai Division.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Shisan came from the Miegunai Division.

sentences.zh: 父鐸魯斡，歷官節度使。

translations.literal: His father Duolugun had served in office as Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duolugun had served as Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十三辨黠，善揣摩人意。

translations.literal: Shisan was discerning and sharp, skilled at reading people's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Shisan was clever and shrewd, adept at reading what others wished to hear.

sentences.zh: 清寧間，以年勞遷護衛太保。

translations.literal: During Qingning, on account of years of service he was transferred to Guards Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingning he was promoted to Guards Commissioner on the strength of long service.

sentences.zh: 大康初，耶律乙辛復入樞府，益橫恣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dakang, Yelü Yixin again entered the Commissioner's Office and grew still more overbearing and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Dakang, Yelü Yixin returned to the Commissioner's Office and grew more domineering than ever.

sentences.zh: 時十三出入乙辛家，以朝臣不附者輒使出之，十三由宿衛遷殿前副點檢。

translations.literal: At that time Shisan went in and out of Yixin's house; whenever court ministers did not attach themselves to him he would have them sent out, and Shisan rose from palace guard duty to Associate Commissioner of the Palace Front Office.
translations.idiomatic: Shisan was constantly at Yixin's house; any courtier who would not join their faction was promptly posted away, and Shisan rose from palace guard to Associate Commissioner of the Palace Front Office.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，護衛蕭忽古等謀殺乙辛，事覺下獄。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year the guardsmen Xiao Hugu and others plotted to kill Yixin; the affair came to light and they were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year the guardsman Xiao Hugu and others plotted to assassinate Yixin; when the plot was discovered they were thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 十三謂乙辛曰：「今太子猶在，臣民屬心。

translations.literal: Shisan said to Yixin, "The crown prince still lives, and officials and people look to him in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Shisan told Yixin, "The crown prince is still alive, and officials and commoners alike look to him.

sentences.zh: 大王素無根柢之助，復有誣皇后之怨。

translations.literal: Your Highness from of old has had no deep-rooted support, and moreover bears the resentment of having framed the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has never had a firm base of support, and you still bear the grudge of having framed the empress.

sentences.zh: 若太子立，王置身何地？

translations.literal: If the crown prince is established, where will Your Highness place himself?
translations.idiomatic: If the crown prince succeeds to the throne, where will that leave Your Highness?

sentences.zh: 宜熟計之。」

translations.literal: You ought to think it through carefully."
translations.idiomatic: You must think this through carefully.

sentences.zh: 乙辛曰：「吾憂此久矣！」

translations.literal: Yixin said, "I have worried about this for a long time!"
translations.idiomatic: Yixin replied, "I have worried about that for a long time!

sentences.zh: 是夜，召蕭得裏特謀所以構太子事。

translations.literal: That night he summoned Xiao Delite to plot how to frame the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: That very night he summoned Xiao Delite to plot how to frame the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 十三計既行，尋遷殿前都點檢，兼同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Once Shisan's plan had been carried out, he was soon transferred to Commissioner of the Palace Front Office and concurrently Associate Administrator of the Commissioner's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shisan's scheme succeeded, he was soon promoted to Commissioner of the Palace Front Office and made Associate Administrator of the Commissioner's Office as well.

sentences.zh: 復令蕭訛都斡等誣首耶律查剌前告耶律撒剌等事皆實，詔究其事。

translations.literal: He again had Xiao Eduo and the rest lodge a false confession that Yelü Chala's earlier accusation against Yelü Sala and the rest was all true, and an edict ordered investigation of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He again had Xiao Eduo and others confess falsely that Yelü Chala's earlier charge against Yelü Sala and his associates had been true, and the emperor ordered a full inquiry.

sentences.zh: 太子不服，別遣夷離畢耶律燕哥問太子，太子具陳所以見誣之狀。

translations.literal: The crown prince would not submit; separately Yilibi Yelü Yangge was sent to question the crown prince, and the prince set forth in full the circumstances of how he had been falsely accused.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince protested his innocence, so Yilibi Yelü Yangge was sent to question him; the prince laid out in detail how he had been framed.

sentences.zh: 十三聞之，謂燕哥曰：「如此奏，則大事去矣，當易其辭為伏款。」

translations.literal: Shisan heard of it and said to Yangge, "If you memorialize in this way, the great affair will be lost; you ought to change his words into a confession of guilt."
translations.idiomatic: When Shisan heard of this he told Yangge, "Report it that way and the whole scheme collapses—you must turn his words into a confession.

sentences.zh: 燕哥入，如十三言奏之。

translations.literal: Yangge entered and memorialized as Shisan had said.
translations.idiomatic: Yangge went in and reported exactly as Shisan had instructed.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，廢太子。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and deposed the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and deposed the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子將出，曰：「我何罪至是！」

translations.literal: As the crown prince was about to go out, he said, "What crime have I committed to come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: As the crown prince was led away he cried, "What crime have I committed to deserve this!

sentences.zh: 十三叱令登車，遣衛卒闔車門。

translations.literal: Shisan shouted at him to mount the carriage and sent guardsmen to shut the carriage door.
translations.idiomatic: Shisan shouted at him to get into the carriage and had guardsmen slam the door shut.

sentences.zh: 是年，遷北院樞密副使，復陳陰害太子計，乙辛從之。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Associate Commissioner of the Northern Commissioner's Office; he again set forth a secret plan to harm the crown prince, and Yixin followed it.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made Associate Commissioner of the Northern Commissioner's Office; he again proposed a secret plot against the crown prince, and Yixin agreed.

sentences.zh: 及乙辛出知南院大王事，亦出十三為保州統軍使，卒。

translations.literal: When Yixin was sent out to serve as Grand Prince of the Southern Commission, Shisan was also sent out as Military Commander of Baozhou and died there.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixin was transferred to Grand Prince of the Southern Commission, Shisan was posted away as Military Commander of Baozhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 乾統間，剖棺戮屍。

translations.literal: During Qiantong his coffin was opened and his corpse was disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiantong era his coffin was opened and his corpse was publicly shamed.

sentences.zh: 二子：的裏得、念經，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: His two sons, Dilede and Nianjing, both submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons, Dilede and Nianjing, were both executed.
